findings.title: Server accepts cipher suites without forward secrecy
findings.why: Static-RSA key exchange means a single future compromise of the private key decrypts every session ever recorded. ECDHE removes that risk.
findings.detail: 3 accepted suites use static RSA key exchange: TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256, TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384.

findings.title: Cookie is missing the HttpOnly flag
findings.why: Without HttpOnly the cookie is readable from JavaScript, so any XSS turns directly into credential theft.
findings.detail: Cookie _octo is readable from JavaScript.

findings.title: Server accepts CBC-mode cipher suites
findings.why: CBC with MAC-then-encrypt has produced a decade of padding-oracle and timing attacks (Lucky13 and successors). AEAD suites have no equivalent history.
findings.detail: 3 accepted suites use CBC mode: TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256, TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256, TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA256.

findings.title: OCSP stapling is not enabled
findings.why: Without stapling the client either skips revocation checking or leaks which site it is visiting to the CA, and pays a round trip for it.
findings.detail: No stapled OCSP response was returned in the handshake. A direct OCSP query returned status good.

findings.title: No Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header
findings.why: Without COOP a page you open, or that opens you, keeps a window reference across origins. That reference is the basis of tabnabbing and of several XS-Leaks.
findings.detail: No Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy header, so cross-origin documents can retain a window reference to this page.

findings.title: No Permissions-Policy header
findings.why: Powerful features stay available to the document and, in some cases, to embedded third-party frames. Denying what you do not use limits what injected or embedded code can reach.
findings.detail: No Permissions-Policy header, so camera, microphone, geolocation and payment keep their default availability.

findings.title: style-src allows 'unsafe-inline'
findings.why: Inline styles enable CSS-based data exfiltration and UI redressing. It is much less severe than inline script and is often impractical to remove, but it is not free.
findings.detail: 'unsafe-inline' is allowed for stylesheets.

findings.title: Session resumption is not offered
findings.why: Resumption is a latency optimisation. Disabling it is a defensible trade-off in exchange for simpler forward-secrecy reasoning.
findings.detail: A second handshake with the same session cache did not resume.

findings.title: No Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy header
findings.why: COEP is only needed if you want crossOriginIsolated (SharedArrayBuffer, precise timers). It breaks third-party embeds that do not opt in, so its absence is reported, not penalised.
findings.detail: No Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy header, so the document is not cross-origin isolated.

findings.title: No Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header
findings.why: CORP tells the browser who may embed this response. It is the cheapest mitigation for Spectre-style cross-origin leaks of resource contents.
findings.detail: No Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy header, so other origins may embed this response.

findings.title: X-Frame-Options is redundant given CSP frame-ancestors
findings.why: Every browser that supports frame-ancestors ignores X-Frame-Options when both are present. Keeping it only helps very old clients; it is not a finding.
findings.detail: X-Frame-Options: DENY is set alongside CSP frame-ancestors, which supersedes it. Keeping it only helps pre-CSP2 browsers.

findings.title: Server header present without a version
findings.why: The product name alone is low-value information. Suppressing it entirely is cheap but optional.
findings.detail: Server names the product but not a version.
findings.subject: Server

findings.title: Server advertises modern protocols over ALPN
findings.why: ALPN negotiation offers HTTP/2.
findings.detail: ALPN negotiated: h2, http/1.1.

findings.title: Certificate and chain are valid
findings.why: The chain verifies, the hostname matches and the certificate is well within its validity window.
findings.detail: Valid until 2026-11-29, chain of 3 verified against the system roots.

findings.title: Server enforces its own cipher suite order
findings.why: The server, not the client, decides which suite is used.
findings.detail: The server selected the same suite regardless of the order the client offered them.

findings.title: Only modern TLS versions are accepted
findings.why: The server speaks TLS 1.2 and/or 1.3 and refuses the deprecated versions.
findings.detail: TLS 1.2 and 1.3 are accepted; 1.0 and 1.1 are refused.
findings.evidence:
TLS 1.0: refused
TLS 1.1: refused
TLS 1.2: accepted (TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256)
TLS 1.3: accepted (TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256)

findings.title: CORS configuration is sound
findings.why: The server does not expose credentialed responses to arbitrary origins.
findings.detail: No Access-Control-Allow-Origin was returned for a foreign origin.

findings.title: Strict-Transport-Security is correctly configured
findings.why: A long max-age with includeSubDomains is enforced.
findings.detail: max-age=31536000 with includeSubDomains.

findings.title: Domain is on the Chrome HSTS preload list
findings.why: Browsers refuse plain HTTP for this host before the first request is ever made.
findings.detail: Found in the embedded Chrome preload subset (updated 2026-09-01).

findings.title: No deprecated security headers
findings.why: The response carries no withdrawn or counterproductive headers.
findings.detail: No withdrawn security headers are sent.

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff is set
findings.why: MIME sniffing is disabled.
findings.detail: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff

findings.title: Referrer-Policy restricts cross-origin referrers
findings.why: Third parties receive at most the origin, never the full URL.
findings.detail: The effective policy is strict-origin-when-cross-origin.

findings.title: CSP sets a restrictive base-uri
findings.why: Injected <base> tags cannot redirect relative script URLs.
findings.detail: base-uri 'self'

findings.title: CSP declares a restrictive default-src
findings.why: Directives that are not listed explicitly fall back to a restrictive default.
findings.detail: default-src 'none'

findings.title: CSP sets a restrictive frame-ancestors
findings.why: Framing is limited to an explicit set of origins.
findings.detail: frame-ancestors 'none'

findings.title: CSP sets object-src 'none'
findings.why: Plugin content is blocked.
findings.detail: default-src 'none'

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy is set
findings.why: A Content-Security-Policy header is enforced by the browser.
findings.detail: An enforced policy with 15 directives is deployed.
